description: Cases for the check. Start from a copy of contracts/ (or an empty directory when `empty` is true), add `files`, write `ledger` to .ledger/<side>.jsonl (write no such file when `noLedger` is true) and `otherLedger` to the other side's ledger, then check `side`. Every implementation must report exactly these problems, in this order, and exactly these hints, word for word. `report` is the whole text the check command prints for the case, character for character (to standard output when there are no problems, to standard error otherwise); in it, {tool} stands for the name of the executable (contract-fixtures in the TypeScript package, contract_fixtures in the Dart package).

cases.case: provider side: everything verified or read
cases.report: {tool} check (provider side): OK (4 fixture(s), all verified or read by this side's tests)

cases.case: consumer side: everything verified or read
cases.report: {tool} check (consumer side): OK (4 fixture(s), all verified or read by this side's tests)

cases.report: {tool} check (provider side): OK (4 fixture(s), all verified or read by this side's tests)

cases.case: provider side: nothing ran
hints: .ledger/provider.jsonl has no entries. Did the provider side's tests run, and do they use this contracts directory?
cases.report:
{tool} check (provider side): 4 problem(s) in 4 fixture(s)
  - provider/order.created.json: not verified by the provider side's tests (stale: delete it, or restore the test that produces it)
  - provider/order.out-of-stock.json: not verified by the provider side's tests (stale: delete it, or restore the test that produces it)
  - consumer/create-order.request.json: not read by the provider side's tests (add a test that feeds it to the real code)
  - tables/order-total.json: not read by the provider side's tests (add a test that feeds it to the real code)
